newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW--Lee Enterprises sees strong Q1.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--Lee Enterprises sees strong Q1.

text.p: Lee Enterprises Inc expects improved results for the December 31 first-quarter over the same year-ago period, Richard Gottlieb, president and chief executive officer, said in a telephone interview.

Gottlieb based his outlook for the Davenport, Iowa-based newspaper and broadcasting company on an easing in newsprint prices, stronger prime time television ratings and a healthy retail environment in its markets.
"Based on these indicators and coming out of the first month (of the quarter), compared to last year we're very optimistic," said Gottlieb.
In the year-ago quarter, Lee Enterprises earned $0.33 per share, down from $0.37 the prior year.
"Last year, we hit the wall in October and November, especially on the broadcast side. The market kind of died on us. That seems to have righted itself," he said.
Lee owns 19 daily newspapers and 40 weekly and specialty publications. It owns and operates nine network affiliated television stations and seven satellite TV stations.
Chris Wahlig, director of finance, said the First Call analysts' consensus earnings estimate for all of fiscal 1997 of $1.35 per share is "not unreasonable."

Lee Enterprises posted earnings from continuing operations for fiscal 1996 of $1.12, which exclude a charge of $0.33 for disposition of a unit and a gain of $0.16 per share from discontinued operations.

Gottlieb said Lee's acquisition strategy involves both niche fill-ins and expansion to new territory. "There are a lot of things on the table, but whether they'll come to fruition ... I can't tell you," he said.

The company will consider both newspaper and broadcasting properties, although Gottlieb said "prices of broadcast properties are awfully high." He added, "We're patient. Cycles change, and we're not going to get caught up in 'everybody's buying, therefore I've got to buy' (syndrome)."
Lee Enterprises was trading unchanged at 23.
